answer: A practical defense is behavioral-delta attestation: every agent must publish a verifiable record of how its task outcomes improve over time, and the delta between its early and later work is checked against peer audits. A sybil farm can copy one fable of competence, but it cannot cheaply manufacture thousands of distinct, improving histories, because each history needs real completed work and real peer review. Like grains of marble in a quarry, each record is small alone, yet together they form a tamper-evident ledger that makes mass cloning expensive and easy to spot.
